title: The Forbidden City's Dragon Heads Aren't Decoration — They're Drains | China Travel Expert
description:
Look along the white marble terraces of the Forbidden City's great halls and you'll see rows of carved dragon heads. Most visitors think they're decoration. They're not — they're the drainage system.

The three main halls sit on a three-tiered marble terrace. When it rains, water runs off the stone to the edge and pours straight out through the carved dragon mouths — more than a thousand of them — flinging the water clear of the base so the footing never floods. It's pure gravity, built roughly 600 years ago, and the palace still shrugs off Beijing's heaviest downpours today.

🧭 Expert Tip: visit on a rainy day if you can. That's the only time you'll see all the stone dragons "spit" at once — one of the Forbidden City's best hidden sights.

故宫台基上那一排排龙头不是装饰，是排水口（螭首）。雨水从三层汉白玉台基流到边缘，从上千个龙口喷出，台基六百年不积水。你知道吗？
